title: Rc Math Smoke
objective: Create a fast authoritative release mathematics smoke corpus spanning ZZ, QQ, GF(p), GF(2), polynomials, extensions, graphs, and modular symbols.

oracles: algebraic reconstruction, inverse, kernel, and serialization invariants

handoff.summary: Added one deterministic, unchanged Sage mathematics program and a release verifier for source-checkout, installed-package, and standalone-executable entry points. Every invocation receives a new HOME, USERPROFILE, XDG cache, temporary directory, and Windows application-data roots; ambient NODE_PATH, NODE_OPTIONS, and Sage.js cache, policy, profile, and source overrides are discarded. Source verification explicitly refuses delegation to an optional workspace SEA. Native evidence uses a closed implementation vocabulary and five named witnesses spanning integer and rational FLINT resources, declared word-prime FFI, M4RI resources, and a lazy compiled typed-Python kernel. POSIX invocations run in a dedicated process group; Windows timeouts use taskkill /T /F and fail closed if tree termination cannot be confirmed. The corpus verifies exact outputs and reconstruction invariants across ZZ, QQ, GF(97), and GF(2) matrices; exact, finite-field, and extension-field polynomials; GF(9); Petersen graph invariants and graph6; modular symbols and Hecke operators; mutation isolation; SagePack round trips; and deterministic lazy-native execution. A cold hermetic linux-x64 source run completes in about 10.5 seconds, within the 30-second release budget.
risks: The tracked test must be added to the integration array in test/node-test-manifest.cjs. That shared file is intentionally outside this lane's claims. Until integration adds the entry, pnpm test:portable fails only its global manifest-completeness assertion; all other 270 portable tests pass.

A stale pre-lane SEA at /home/user/sagejs/build/sea/sagejs failed the unchanged corpus at exact ZZ polynomial gcd. This is useful release-drift detection, not a reason to weaken the corpus; newly built artifacts must pass it.

This lane's recorded execution evidence is linux-x64. Linux exercises the real POSIX process-group timeout. CI or a release lane must run the same descendant-timeout regression on Windows x64 to prove taskkill /T /F behavior, and must run artifact mathematics on Linux ARM64 and macOS ARM64.
next_steps: Register test/release-math-smoke.cjs in the integration array of test/node-test-manifest.cjs and rerun pnpm test:portable after integration.
Run scripts/release-math-smoke.cjs --require-native against each clean npm installation and every newly built standalone artifact.
Archive each JSON report beside the corresponding release manifest so release review retains exact mathematics and native-selection evidence.
